kit.installHint: A plain folder such as C:\VRRealmsCreatorKit works best. Desktop and Documents can be guarded by security software that blocks updates.

help.title: Help
help.discordLead: Creators and the VR Realms team help each other there. Share a screenshot of what you see and what you expected.
help.docsLead: Step-by-step guides for maps, avatars, items and uploads.
help.faq1q: Do I need Visual Studio or C++?
help.faq1a: No. The kit comes ready to use: Unreal Engine 5.8 and a Steam account that owns VR Realms are enough.
help.faq2q: Will an update touch my maps or avatars?
help.faq2a: No. Updates only change the kit's own files, never the Community folder where your work lives. Every file an update replaces is copied into a _VRRUpdaterBackup_ folder first.
help.faq3q: The update says Windows will not let it replace a file.
help.faq3a: Close Unreal Editor. If it still happens, security software is guarding the folder: allow this app in it, or keep the kit in a plain folder such as C:\VRRealmsCreatorKit.
help.faq4q: Upload says Steam did not upload anything.
help.faq4a: Sign SteamCMD in once from the Home page (Steam sign-in for uploads), with the name you log in to Steam with.

creations.emptyTitle: Nothing on the Workshop yet. Get building!
creations.emptyLead: Make a world or an avatar in the Creator Kit and press Upload in its Workshop panel. It shows up here, with how many players visit it, wear it and rate it.

creations.noAccountTitle: No Steam account found on this PC
creations.noAccountLead: Sign in to Steam, then press Refresh. The app finds your creations from the Steam account on this PC.
creations.offline: Your creations could not be loaded: {{error}}
creations.footnote: Players are counted from the game over the last 90 days, and your own visits are not. A world counts the players who were in it; an avatar counts the players who wore it in worlds or the hub. Ratings, comments and subscribers come from Steam. Private, friends-only and unlisted items are not listed.
